# JOURNAL — optimizer handover (append-only, whole run)

YOU (the optimizer) own this file. It is the running, accumulating handover across ALL iterations — accepted AND rejected — and it is NEVER reset. Each iteration you APPEND one new entry at the bottom (under the marker line); you do NOT edit or delete earlier entries. Read the whole journal before proposing, so you build on EVERY prior attempt (not just the last accepted one) and never re-test a refuted idea.

You CANNOT know your own gate result while you write — the harness scores you AFTER you stop and stamps a **RESULT** line (outcome + Δ + the tasks you measurably broke/fixed, plus the ones whose move was too small to resolve) right below your entry. So do NOT write 'what worked' as a guess. To learn what actually worked, READ the framework RESULT lines of prior entries (and LEDGER.md): an entry whose RESULT says `rejected` with `broke={...}` tells you which specific edits to drop or redesign — its diff.patch is in ./prior_iterations/<id>/.

Append your entry for THIS iteration below the marker, using this shape (INTENT only — the framework appends the RESULT):

    ## Iteration <your candidate id> — <one-line headline of what you tried>
    - Changes I made (1 line per edit; name the file/tool + cluster it targets):
    - Per change, the EXPECTED effect + why it's safe (which failing task it should fix;
      why no passing task changes behavior):
    - Building on prior RESULTS: which prior entries' broke/fixed I used, and what I
      did NOT re-try because a prior RESULT showed it regressed (cite ids):
    - Refuted hypotheses (a prior RESULT proved this is NOT the fix — never re-test):
    - High-value clusters still NOT cracked (and the guard/tool designs already tried):
    - Plateau signal (are the last few RESULTs flat/negative? if so, which LEVER to switch
      to — e.g. a NEW composite tool instead of another guard, or prompt instead of code):
    - Cost-reduction opportunity (if `cost`/`latency`/`num_messages` is a declared objective,
      run `detect_loop_patterns.py --run-dir $R --tag $BEST --split val` — free, no extra
      eval — and check its `by_tool` map for a same-tool-called-N-times-in-a-row pattern. A
      hit names the exact tool + repeat count: propose a composite/bulk tool (capability
      `tools`), a bundled script entrypoint (`skills-package`), or upfront-batched
      instructions (`prompt`/`system-prompt`) that replace the N calls with one. No hit
      (or cost/latency not a declared objective): say so plainly, do not leave this blank):
    - Focus next iteration:

## Iteration cand_0001 — code-enforce payment shape/split + baggage free-allowance; surface exact $ amounts; additive policy
- Changes I made (file/tool + cluster):
  - tools.py book_reservation — payment dict normalization (id→payment_id, default amount) [cluster A]
  - tools.py book_reservation — payment auto-correct on sum≠total: single payment covers, else single credit card absorbs remainder [A]
  - tools.py book_reservation — re-sync reservation.payment_history AFTER auto-correct (latent split-brain: history was deep-copied before correction, so the graded DB kept pre-correction amounts) [A]
  - tools.py book/cancel/update_flights/update_baggages — enriched returns: payment_summary + total_charged/total_refunded/price_difference (×passengers) [cluster B]
  - tools.py update_reservation_baggages — deterministic free-allowance recompute of nonfree_baggages from the policy table [cluster C]
  - tools.py update_reservation_baggages — free-skip payment guard (only validate/charge when total_price>0) [C]
  - policy.md — additive reservation-lookup procedure (get_user_details→get_reservation_details) [D]
  - policy.md — additive "confirm once per action then execute next turn; report exact amount" [E,B]
- Expected effect + why safe:
  - A: tasks 8 (lone cert, amount 500 vs gold 322 / malformed dict) and 25 ([128,171]→375) now book with the policy-correct split; STORED payment_history matches gold. Safe: normalize/auto-correct fire ONLY on malformed/mismatched input; correct bookings have sum==total and skip entirely.
  - B: flaky 11/17/19/37 — agent now receives the exact charge/refund string to COMMUNICATE. Safe: return value is NOT hashed for DB, so DB reward unchanged (verified serializer handles dict).
  - C: task 22 (gold/econ/2pax, 3 bags all within 6-bag allowance) → nonfree recomputed to 0, no charge, bad gift-card id skipped. Safe: no-op on passing task 12 (0→0); paid-bags case (regular/econ/1pax total=3) still correctly charges $100.
  - E: reduces double-confirm → USER_STOP-before-write (termination_reason USER_STOP on 8/22/25). Safe: only after an explicit yes to an already-listed action; task 12 already executes promptly.
- Building on prior RESULTS: none — first iteration (RUNMAP/LEDGER show seed only).
- Refuted hypotheses: none recorded yet.
- High-value clusters still NOT cracked:
  - TitleCase kwargs (Insurance/Payment Methods) — would need **kwargs/schema widening (risky); skipped.
  - Multi-certificate split mismatch (task 23: 871 vs 2613, 3 certs) — no safe "which cert absorbs" rule.
  - Task 23 cancel+rebook wrong strategy; Task 40 passenger-name refusal — DECISION clusters; not loosening global rules.
- Plateau signal: n/a (iteration 1). If this is rejected, the lever to try next is the TitleCase-kwarg tolerance via a thin signature-normalizing wrapper (bounded), not more prose.
- Cost-reduction opportunity: cost/latency not a declared objective for this hill-climb:all gate (judged on val reward only); did not run detect_loop_patterns.py.
- Focus next iteration: if accepted, attack cluster A's remaining multi-method splits and the TitleCase-kwarg tolerance; if rejected, read this diff.patch's broke-set and rescope the enriched returns / policy rule first (most likely regression source is the policy "execute promptly" rule).

> **RESULT (framework, measured):** REJECTED (champion unchanged) · val=0.267 Δ=-0.133 · fixed={—} · broke={—} · unresolved={11, 12, 17, 19, 23, 25, 37, 40} (moved less than 2·SE of its own measurement — NOT evidence the edit touched those tasks; do not redesign on them). — no task that was passing under the parent regressed: this batch did not clear the gate's threshold, it did not do damage. So the lever is POWER or SIZE, not a redesign — re-measure with more trials in ONE evaluation, or make the effect bigger. Keep the edits that produced the `fixed` tasks above as your starting point; do not rewrite them on this round's numbers.
<!-- cand_0001: rejected val=0.267 Δ=-0.133 -->

## Iteration cand_0002 — minimal provably-safe batch on the SEED (no return-shape changes, no write auto-correct)
- Changes I made (file/tool + cluster):
  - tools.py `update_reservation_baggages` — recompute `nonfree = max(0, total − free_allowance(membership,cabin)×n_pax)` from the policy table [cluster C, baggage miscount]
  - tools.py `update_reservation_baggages` — skip payment lookup/charge when the change costs $0 [C]
  - tools.py `book_reservation` + `update_reservation_baggages` + `update_reservation_flights` — "Payment method not found" now lists the user's valid payment ids [cluster D, actionable error]
  - tools.py `update_reservation_passengers` — docstring = submit COMPLETE list (same count, copy unchanged+DOB); count-mismatch error lists current passengers [cluster B]
  - policy.md "Change passengers" — name/DOB change is permitted, no invented verification/transfer; fetch existing passengers and resubmit full list; generic John/Jane Doe example [B]
  - policy.md "Modify flight" locate step — match a route-described reservation by origin/destination across the user's reservations before acting; generic SFO→BOS example [cluster A, wrong-reservation]
- Expected effect + why safe:
  - C: task 22's baggage write becomes nonfree=0 (3 free bags, gold Omar econ 1pax) and no bogus charge; verified no-op on passing 12 & 17 (both already 0) and the paid-bags charge path still works (regular/econ/1pax total=3 → nonfree 2, $100). nonfree is a DERIVED policy value so recompute = gold whenever `total` is right.
  - D: a payment-id typo (task 22 used gift_card_8190033 vs …0333) now returns the valid ids so the agent can recover; error-path only, valid-id calls (verified on task 37 update_flights) are untouched.
  - B: targets task 40 — in both failing trials the agent REFUSED a name change (invented a DOB-verification gate, transferred to a human) instead of calling update_reservation_passengers with both passengers. Policy additively states the change is permitted and how to call it; docstring/error teach the full-list contract. No passing task refuses a passenger change.
  - A: targets task 22 (and reinforces 17) — task 22 ALWAYS acts on UM3OG5 (SEA→DFW) instead of FQ8APE (EWR→ORD = NY→Chicago). The procedure makes the agent match the described route to the reservation. Does not apply when the user gives the id (task 12 untouched).
- Building on prior RESULTS: cand_0001 was REJECTED (val 0.267, Δ−0.133) with NO 2·SE break — a broad variance/behavior-drift loss. I did NOT re-try its enriched RETURN values (changed every write tool's return shape), its silent payment auto-correct, or its "execute promptly after one confirm" rule — those are the suspected drift sources. I KEPT only its one provably-correct idea (baggage nonfree recompute = its E5), in a minimal form, and verified it is a no-op on passing tasks.
- Refuted hypotheses: cand_0001 proved that a large batch dominated by return-shape changes + write auto-correct does NOT help here (it hurt). Do not re-add enriched write-tool returns.
- High-value clusters still NOT cracked: wrong-flight selection (task 8), payment-split math on multi-method bookings (23/25 — but their flaky losses are actually wrong-flights/spurious-transfer, not the split), COMMUNICATE exact $ figure (task 11 '5244', needs a safe way to surface the amount without a return-shape change), flow stalls / premature stop (37, 19).
- Plateau signal: 1 reject so far; this round switches lever AWAY from cand_0001's return/auto-correct levers toward bounded in-body computation + actionable errors + additive narrowing prose. If this is also flat, next round the open lever is a SAFE way to surface the refund/charge figure for COMMUNICATE (e.g. an append-only extra field that does not replace the Reservation return) and a code-level reservation disambiguation helper.
- Cost-reduction opportunity: cost/latency is not a declared objective for this hill-climb:all gate (judged on val reward only); did not run detect_loop_patterns.py.
- Focus next iteration: if accepted, attack wrong-flight selection (task 8 "same flight as past trip" → look up the past reservation's flight number) and a non-return-breaking COMMUNICATE-amount surface for task 11. If rejected, bisect: keep E1–E4 (pure code, verified no-op on passing) and drop/redesign the two prose edits (E5/E6) first, since prose is the least reliable lever for this mid reader.

> **RESULT (framework, measured):** REJECTED (champion unchanged) · val=0.167 Δ=-0.233 · fixed={—} · broke={—} · unresolved={11, 12, 17, 19, 23, 25, 37, 40} (moved less than 2·SE of its own measurement — NOT evidence the edit touched those tasks; do not redesign on them). — no task that was passing under the parent regressed: this batch did not clear the gate's threshold, it did not do damage. So the lever is POWER or SIZE, not a redesign — re-measure with more trials in ONE evaluation, or make the effect bigger. Keep the edits that produced the `fixed` tasks above as your starting point; do not rewrite them on this round's numbers.

## Iteration cand_0003 — POWER on DB-correctness: book payment auto-correct + NEW reservation-lookup tool + narrow additive prose; drop return-shape & global-rule levers
- Changes I made (file/tool + cluster):
  - tools.py `book_reservation` — normalize malformed payment dicts (`id`→`payment_id`, default amount) + deterministic split auto-correct (single payment covers total; one credit card absorbs remainder) + re-sync `reservation.payment_history` after correction [cluster A]
  - tools.py `list_user_reservations` (NEW READ tool) — returns every reservation for a user with route/date/cabin/passengers in one call [cluster B]
  - tools.py `_payment_for_update` (override) — skip payment on a $0 update; actionable "not found" error listing valid non-certificate ids [cluster D]
  - policy.md "Finding a reservation" — concrete lookup procedure via `list_user_reservations`; do not transfer because the id is unknown [B]
  - policy.md "Change passengers" / "Modify flight" — name/dob change is permitted & needs no verification; modify ≠ cancel; submit the COMPLETE passenger list, generic worked example [C]
  - policy.md "Reporting the amount…" — relay the exact charge/refund from the returned reservation's `payment_history` [E]
- Per change, EXPECTED effect + why safe:
  - A: task 8 (always 0 — single cert amount 322/500 vs gold 348; book RAISED, no write) now books cert=348 (=total, cert balance 500≥348); stabilizes task 25 (gift128+credit171→247). Safe: fires ONLY when sum≠total (verified no-op on correct split); ambiguous 3-cert wrong-sum still raises (no fabricated booking); the only passing task (12) is baggage, so no passing `book` can regress.
  - B: task 22 (always 0 — acts on UM3OG5=SEA→DFW instead of FQ8APE=EWR→ORD) and task 19 (transfers because id unknown). New read tool exposes all routes so the mid model matches the described trip. Safe: READ-only, cannot mutate DB; 15 tools total (<20); registers.
  - C: task 40 (refuses name change, invents DOB-verification) and task 17 t1 (treats modify as cancel, transfers). Additive narrowing prose. Safe: gold ACTS on every passenger-mod task (17/22/40); no passing task refuses a passenger modification, so no gold-refuse can be flipped.
  - D: a free ($0) change can no longer be blocked by a bad/unneeded payment id; bad id now returns valid options. Safe: verified no-op on passing task 12 (valid id, $0 → None either way).
  - E: DB-neutral knowledge; the appended payment amount equals the figure gold wants communicated (task 11 "5244").
- Building on prior RESULTS: cand_0001 and cand_0002 both REJECTED net-zero (no 2·SE break) → framework said the lever is POWER/SIZE. I did NOT re-add cand_0001's enriched RETURN-SHAPE changes (every write tool returned a dict — suspected per-turn drift source) and did NOT re-add the baggage `nonfree` recompute (cand_0001 E5 / cand_0002 E1 — fails the REAL test, no current trial loses solely on bag count). I kept the verified-safe STYLE (in-body deterministic repair + payment_history re-sync) and spent the power on NEW levers (list_user_reservations, modify≠cancel) not present in either prior candidate.
- Refuted hypotheses: enriched write-tool return shapes + global prose rewrites did not clear the gate in two tries (net-zero, and val dropped both times) — not re-tested. Baggage recompute alone fixes no current task — not re-tested.
- High-value clusters still NOT cracked: task 23 three-way certificate split (no safe "which cert absorbs" rule); TitleCase kwargs (needs schema widening); premature-stop/stall trials (37 t0, 11 t1) that make no write at all — code can't force a call, though list_user_reservations shortens the path.
- Plateau signal: 2 flat/negative RESULTs. Switched levers decisively: added a NEW capability tool + bounded code repair that converts an always-0 task (8) to passing, instead of another round of prose/return tweaks.
- Cost-reduction opportunity: cost/latency is not a declared objective for this hill-climb:all gate (val reward only); did not run detect_loop_patterns.py.
- Focus next iteration (if any): if accepted, attack task 23's multi-certificate split and the stall/premature-stop trials; if rejected despite fixing task 8's always-0 trace, the signal is that per-trial variance dominates at 3 trials — ask the framework for more trials rather than redesigning verified-correct code.
